predecessors.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

successors.name: Brazilian Republic
successors.text: the whole Acre region: Castro's forces 'had taken the entire region' by 24 January 1903

ledger.x: 14 July 1899: Luis Galvez proclaims the Republic of Acre at Puerto Alonso.
14 July 1899: the rebels contest Bolivian rule in Acre (mirror of the Bolivia dossier).
15 March 1900: Brazil ends the first republic.
6 August 1902: Placido de Castro takes Xapuri.
24-27 January 1903: Acre is in rebel hands.
17 November 1903: the Treaty of Petropolis ends the contest.
17 November 1903: the republic is absorbed into Brazil.

wars.name: Acre War
wars.outcome: Brazil won: the rebel republics were dissolved (1900), defeated (December 1900) or absorbed (1903) and the Treaty of Petropolis of 17 November 1903 gave Acre to Brazil.

certainty.note: No frontier: the rebels held the upper Acre River and, in 1903, 'the entire region'; the page gives no area.
